name: EU Blue Card

qualifying_event.description: A separate combined work-and-residence permit (implementing the EU Blue Card Directive) for highly qualified third-country nationals with a university degree (3+ years) or, for IT/service-management roles, equivalent professional experience, and a job offer meeting the salary threshold.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: University degree (3+ year programme) or IT/service-management professional-experience evidence; job offer meeting salary threshold; employer declaration.

requirements.blocker_text: Gross annual salary (including special payments) must be at least the average gross annual income of full-time employees -- EUR 55,678 for 2026.

A university/tertiary degree of at least 3 years' duration is required, unless applying for an IT/service-management role, where 3+ years of relevant professional experience within the last 7 years may substitute.

evidence_required.document: University degree certificate or IT professional-experience evidence
Employment contract meeting the salary threshold

outcome.duration_length: 24 months, tied to a specific employer

sources.title: migration.gv.at -- EU Blue Card: 2026 salary threshold (EUR 55,678/year), degree/IT-experience requirement, 3 application channels, upgrade to Red-White-Red Card Plus after 21 months of qualifying employment within 24 months

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Austria). Modeled as a distinct route from at_work_permit.json (Red-White-Red Card) since the EU Blue Card has a separate EU-directive legal basis, a flat salary threshold rather than a points system, and its own upgrade path (to Red-White-Red Card Plus after 21/24 months, granting unrestricted labour-market access) confirmed directly on the tier-1 source. work_rights modeled 'restricted' for the same employer-tie reason as at_work_permit.json.
